Theme 095 · Camera & edit grammar

Split Screen

A 1970s split-screen grammar rebuilt for software: hard ink gutters divide the frame into simultaneous views. The hook drowns in six dashboards at once, the drop slams one gutter aside for Acme Pulse, the proof runs three synchronised cameras (Pulse, the chart, the on-call human) on the same timecode, and the gutters close for the lockup.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Ink gutters — 12 px hard dividers; their position is the edit (moving the gutter = cutting)
  • Dashboard panel — one metric per panel with a TAB nn/38 badge; the currency of the hook
  • Camera labels — CAM A / B / C mono tags naming what each panel is watching
  • Synced timecode — amber 09:42:07 chip repeated in every panel to prove simultaneity
  • Decision panel — full-width bottom panel with the anomaly line and Roll back / Acknowledge
  • Split tagline — tagline broken across two panels, then merged into one lockup band

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Panel pop-in — each panel wipes in from its gutter edge (clip-path inset 100% → 0, 0.2 s power3.out), one per eighth note (0.25 s at 120 BPM)
  • Gutter slam — gutter x moves 50% → 33% in 0.18 s with expo.in and a 2-frame overshoot, landing exactly on the drop; the losing panel desaturates to 30%
  • Gutter close — all gutters slide to 0 width over one bar (2 s, power2.inOut) while the panels’ content scales 1 → 0.96; the merged band settles on the downbeat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Split screen shows cause and effect at the same instant, which is exactly what a monitoring product promises: the metric, the alert and the human decision are all visible together. It’s also cheap to build from real UI captures. Risk: on a phone at 1:1 more than three panels becomes noise, and a split that doesn’t say where to look loses the viewer.

Adapt to your product: Put the before-state (your users’ current juggling) in many small panels and your product in one big one. For the proof, split the frame into the three roles your product connects, for example the signal, the system and the person, and keep the same timecode in each.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split_screen_(film) (split screen history and definition) · https://www.premiumbeat.com/blog/split-screen-editing-and-composing/ (composing split screens to guide attention)
